loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

The call ends your run, so do everything else first and put everything your caller needs in that one report. It is not a messaging channel: do not use it for progress updates or questions.

Only a report delivered through SubagentHandback reaches your caller; plain text you write at the end of your run is NOT delivered. There is no recipient parameter: the report can only go to your caller.

addedLines: - agent-skills:accessibility-auditor: Accessibility engineer focused on WCAG compliance, assistive technology support, and inclusive design. Use for accessibility-focused code review, screen-reader and keyboard-navigation auditing, contrast validation, and remediation guidance. (Tools: All tools)

- agent-skills:code-reviewer: Senior code reviewer that evaluates changes across five dimensions — correctness, readability, architecture, security, and performance. Use for thorough code review before merge. (Tools: All tools)

- agent-skills:security-auditor: Security engineer focused on vulnerability detection, threat modeling, and secure coding practices. Use for security-focused code review, threat analysis, or hardening recommendations. (Tools: All tools)

- agent-skills:test-engineer: QA engineer specialized in test strategy, test writing, and coverage analysis. Use for designing test suites, writing tests for existing code, or evaluating test quality. (Tools: All tools)

- agent-skills:web-performance-auditor: Web performance engineer focused on Core Web Vitals, loading, rendering, and network optimization. Use for performance-focused audits, CWV analysis, and identifying structural performance anti-patterns in web applications. (Tools: All tools)

- ai-engineer: Build LLM applications, RAG systems, and prompt pipelines. Implements vector search, agent orchestration, and AI API integrations. Use PROACTIVELY for LLM features, chatbots, or AI-powered applications. (Tools: All tools)

"""Line-aware reader for a PowerCenter XML export.

Every element keeps its start and end line, so facts can cite real line numbers.
VALUEPAIR elements (where the demo's command task keeps a plaintext credential)
are kept as empty nodes: their attributes are dropped at parse time and never
reach any caller.
"""
import re
import xml.parsers.expat

REDACT_TAGS = {"VALUEPAIR"}


class Node:
    __slots__ = ("tag", "a", "start", "end", "children", "parent")

    def __init__(self, tag, a, start, parent):
        self.tag, self.a, self.start, self.end = tag, a, start, start
        self.children, self.parent = [], parent

    def get(self, k, d=None):
        return self.a.get(k, d)

    def kids(self, tag=None):
        return [c for c in self.children if tag is None or c.tag == tag]

    def iter(self, tag=None):
        if tag is None or self.tag == tag:
            yield self
        for c in self.children:
            yield from c.iter(tag)

    def attrs_table(self, child="TABLEATTRIBUTE"):
        return {c.get("NAME"): (c.get("VALUE"), c.start) for c in self.kids(child)}

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<{self.tag} {self.get('NAME', '')} L{self.start}-{self.end}>"


def parse(path):
    data = open(path, "rb").read()
    p = xml.parsers.expat.ParserCreate()
    root = Node("#doc", {}, 1, None)
    stack = [root]

    def start(tag, attrs):
        line = p.CurrentLineNumber
        n = Node(tag, {} if tag in REDACT_TAGS else dict(attrs), line, stack[-1])
        stack[-1].children.append(n)
        stack.append(n)

    def end(tag):
        stack.pop().end = p.CurrentLineNumber

    p.StartElementHandler, p.EndElementHandler = start, end
    # The export declares a DTD (powrmart.dtd) that is not shipped; ignore it.
    p.SetParamEntityParsing(xml.parsers.expat.XML_PARAM_ENTITY_PARSING_NEVER)
    p.Parse(data, True)
    return root.children[0]


def secret_tokens(path):
    """Tokens that appear only on credential lines, for output guards. Never print these."""
    lines = open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read().splitlines()
    sec = [l for l in lines if "VALUEPAIR" in l]
    rest = "\n".join(l for l in lines if "VALUEPAIR" not in l)
    return {t for l in sec for t in re.findall(r"[^\s\"'=;&]{6,}", l) if t not in rest}

# Flowline PowerCenter Demo — Jaffle Shop

A single Informatica PowerCenter repository export (`FLOWLINE_DEMO_JAFFLESHOP.xml`) that reimplements the dbt [Jaffle Shop](https://github.com/dbt-labs/jaffle-shop) demo project as a PowerCenter pipeline. Used for demo purposes only.

## Contents

The export contains one repository (`REPO_Jaffleshop`) and folder (`FLOWLINE_DEMO_JAFFLESHOP`) targeting Oracle, with:

- **Sources** — `RAW_*` tables (customers, orders, items, products, supplies, stores) plus staged `STG_*` tables.
- **Targets** — staging tables (`STG_*`), core marts (`CUSTOMERS`, `ORDERS`, `ORDER_ITEMS`, `PRODUCTS`, `SUPPLIES`), and enriched marts (`CUSTOMER_360`, `ORDER_FINANCIALS`, `ORDER_ITEM_ENRICHED`, `PRODUCT_DAILY_PERFORMANCE`, `STORE_DAILY_KPIS`).
- **Mappings** — `m_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL`, `m_FL_JS_MARTS_CORE`, `m_FL_JS_MARTS_ENRICHED`.
- **Workflow** — `wf_FL_JAFFLESHOP_DEMO`, running the three mappings via sessions `s_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL`, `s_FL_JS_MARTS_CORE`, `s_FL_JS_MARTS_ENRICHED`.

The pipeline flows RAW → staging → core marts → enriched marts.

## Usage

Import `FLOWLINE_DEMO_JAFFLESHOP.xml` into a PowerCenter repository via the Repository Manager or `pmrep`.

input.content:
# Adversarial check of the 20 "problems in the input XML" and the 6 "clean" statements

Sources: the claims in `docs/assets/input-data.js` (problems + clean), the XML
`external/flowline-pwc-demo/FLOWLINE_DEMO_JAFFLESHOP.xml` (4,701 lines), jaffle-shop, and the seed data in
`q.duckdb` (schema `raw`, DuckDB 2.0.1, opened read-only).

Method: my own scripts in this folder. `h.py` is a helper built on pcxml.parse. `lineage.py` is a column-lineage
tracer. `p*.py` are one-off XML checks and `q.py` runs SQL. I did not open input_checks.py, build_input_data.py,
docs/*.html, agent_log.md or any transcript. Every grep of the XML went through `grep -v VALUEPAIR`.

Verdict scale: CONFIRMED (everything checkable is right), PARTLY WRONG (at least one statement is inaccurate
or overstated), WRONG, UNVERIFIABLE.

Every cited line number was printed and read. All of them hold what the text says, so I don't repeat
"line OK" below unless something is off.

---

## 1. swap: "Columns wired into the wrong target column, in 4 places". CONFIRMED

- L608–613 (STG_ORDERS): `SRT_ORDERS.SUBTOTAL -> SUBTOTAL_CENTS`, `TAX_PAID -> TAX_PAID_CENTS`,
  `ORDER_TOTAL -> ORDER_TOTAL_CENTS`, `SUBTOTAL_CENTS -> SUBTOTAL`, `TAX_PAID_CENTS -> TAX_PAID`,
  `ORDER_TOTAL_CENTS -> ORDER_TOTAL`. In EXP_ORDERS, SUBTOTAL = `SUBTOTAL_IN/100` (L111) and SUBTOTAL_CENTS =
  `SUBTOTAL_IN` (L114). So dollars go into the `*_CENTS` columns and cents into the dollar columns. Confirmed.
- L620–621 (STG_PRODUCTS): `PRODUCT_PRICE (PRICE/100) -> PRODUCT_PRICE_CENTS` and
  `PRODUCT_PRICE_CENTS (PRICE) -> PRODUCT_PRICE`. Confirmed.
- L2480–2482 (CUSTOMER_360): SPEND -> PRETAX, PRETAX -> TAX_PAID, TAX_PAID -> SPEND. Confirmed.
- L2542–2543 (PDP): PERISHABLE_SALES_FLAG -> MARGIN_PCT and MARGIN_PCT -> PERISHABLE_SALES_FLAG. Confirmed.
- "in 4 places": I checked every connector into a target whose source port name differs from the target
  column (p3.py). Exactly these 4 groups are swaps. The rest are harmless renames (ID -> CUSTOMER_ID,
  *_CL -> plain names). I also checked connectors into non-targets: the only name changes are the
  `*_RECAL -> SUBTOTAL/TAX_PAID/ORDER_TOTAL` renames at L4005–4007, which are not swaps.
- "joined by position": this is an inference, not something the XML records. It does fit all 4 cases: the
  upstream port order lines up with the target column order (for example SRT_ORDERS lists SUBTOTAL, TAX_PAID,
  ORDER_TOTAL, SUBTOTAL_CENTS… while the target lists SUBTOTAL_CENTS, TAX_PAID_CENTS, ORDER_TOTAL_CENTS,
  SUBTOTAL…).
- Suggested wording: "In each case the port order matches the target's column order, which suggests the
  ports were linked by position."

## 2. round: "Two of the swaps also lose data in the original database". PARTLY WRONG

- L1087: PERISHABLE_SALES_FLAG is `number(p,s)` with precision 1 and scale 0. L73: TAX_PAID_CENTS is
  `number(15,0)`. Confirmed.
- "61,296 of 61,948 orders have tax that is not a whole dollar". `select count(*) filter (where tax_paid % 100
  <> 0) from raw.raw_orders` gives 61,296 of 61,948. Confirmed.
- **Overstated:** "Tax in dollars (like 0.42) … so it becomes 0." Rounding to a whole number gives 0 only when
  the tax is under $0.50. The query `count(*) filter (where tax_paid < 50)` returns **45,658 orders → 0**, and
  `tax_paid >= 50` returns **16,290 orders → 1 to 6** (max tax is 594 cents). Of those, 225 are exactly x.50.
- MARGIN_PCT -> NUMBER(1,0): "becomes 0 or 1" holds for a ratio between 0 and 1. With the seed data and the
  swap, MARGIN_PCT works out to 1 − (supply cost in dollars)/(price in cents). That is 0.9965–0.9989 for every
  product (query over raw_products and raw_supplies), so **every PDP row would get 1**. The example "0.6543" is
  only an illustration.
- Missing: two more swaps put dollars into `number(15,0)` columns. STG_ORDERS.SUBTOTAL_CENTS (L72) gets
  dollar subtotals and STG_PRODUCTS.PRODUCT_PRICE_CENTS (L56) gets dollar prices. They lose nothing today only
  because every seed subtotal and price is a whole dollar (`subtotal % 100 <> 0` gives 0 rows, and prices are
  400–1400). So "two" is right for the seed data, but four columns are at risk in general. ORDER_TOTAL_CENTS
  is `number(12,2)` and loses nothing.
- Semantics: Oracle rounds to the column's scale when a value is inserted into NUMBER(p,0). I have not tested
  whether PowerCenter converts the value itself first (bulk mode, "Enable high precision" = NO at L1007). So
  "the database rounds it" is very likely right, but I have not tested it.
- Suggested wording: "Tax in dollars lands in TAX_PAID_CENTS, a NUMBER(15,0) column (L73), so it is rounded to
  a whole number: 0 for 45,658 orders and 1–6 for the other 16,290. MARGIN_PCT lands in PERISHABLE_SALES_FLAG,
  NUMBER(1,0) (L1087). With the seed data every margin is about 0.997, so the column is 1 on every row.
  SUBTOTAL_CENTS and PRODUCT_PRICE_CENTS are also NUMBER(15,0) and get dollars; they lose nothing today only
  because seed prices are whole dollars."

## 3. spread: "The staging swaps spread into the marts". CONFIRMED (with one note)

- My own lineage tracer (lineage.py) follows connectors, expression references, Router REF_FIELD and Union
  FIELDDEPENDENCY back from every mart target column. It flags columns that depend on STG_ORDERS
  {SUBTOTAL, TAX_PAID, ORDER_TOTAL and their *_CENTS columns} or STG_PRODUCTS {PRODUCT_PRICE, PRODUCT_PRICE_CENTS}.
  Result: **40 columns in 9 tables** (out of 130 mart columns). The column list is **identical** to the
  claim's list, table by table.
- L3534: `SUBTOTAL_RECAL = SUBTOTAL_CENTS/100` reaches ORDERS.SUBTOTAL through L4005 and L3783.
  STG_ORDERS.SUBTOTAL_CENTS holds dollars, so the result is 100 times too small. Confirmed. (ORDERS.TAX_PAID is
  worse, because TAX_PAID_CENTS was already rounded.)
- L1614: EFFECTIVE_TAX_RATE = TAX_PAID / SUBTOTAL. In the enriched mapping both inputs come from STG_ORDERS.TAX_PAID
  and SUBTOTAL (L2740–2741), which both hold cents and were not rounded. So the ratio is right. Confirmed.
- Note (missing, not wrong): the swap also changes 4 columns through the Router condition rather than through
  the data flow: ORDER_FINANCIALS.ORDER_VALUE_BAND, STORE_DAILY_KPIS.HIGH_VALUE_ORDERS, STORE_DAILY_KPIS.HIGH_VALUE_ORDERS_PCT
  and CUSTOMER_360.HIGH_VALUE_ORDERS. These are all "HIGH" or the full count because of problem 7. "Computed
  from" is accurate as a lineage statement, but readers may take the 40 as every column the swap affects.
- Also: some of the 40 come out numerically right anyway (EFFECTIVE_TAX_RATE). RFM_SEGMENT does not change
  today because R_SCORE is always 1, as problem 9 explains.

## 4. counter: "The per-customer order counter never restarts". CONFIRMED

- L3588: `v_PREV_CUSTOMER_ID = CUSTOMER_ID`. L3589: `v_ORDER_SEQUENCE = IIF(v_PREV_CUSTOMER_ID = CUSTOMER_ID,
  v_ORDER_SEQUENCE + 1, 1)`. L1705–1706 is the same pair in the enriched mapping. Confirmed.
- L3790 (core) and L2496 (enriched, writing to instance ORDER_FINANCIALS1) carry CUSTOMER_ORDER_NUMBER to the
  targets. Confirmed.
- Semantics: PowerCenter evaluates input ports, then variable ports in display order, then output ports. A
  variable that refers to itself sees the previous row's value, and a numeric variable starts at 0. This comes
  from documentation (Transformation Guide, port order), not a test. Given that, the comparison is TRUE on every
  row, so the counter runs 1…N in sorted order. The only exception would be a NULL CUSTOMER_ID: then NULL = NULL
  goes to the false branch and the counter resets to 1. The seed has no NULL customer (0 rows), and every row
  on this path comes from a matched join.
- jaffle-shop's `customer_order_number` is a `row_number()` per customer (orders.sql L68–71). Confirmed.

## 5. firstcustomer: "The first-customer flag is always 0". CONFIRMED

- L2124–2126 set v_PREV_LOCATION/DAY/CUSTOMER to the current row. L2127 compares them with the current row and
  returns 0 when they match. With the same port-order semantics, all three always match, so the flag is 0.
- L2004 `UNIQUE_CUSTOMERS = SUM(IS_FIRST_CUSTOMER)`, fed through L2940, reaches STORE_DAILY_KPIS through L2549.
  Confirmed.
- "Only a row with an empty location, day or customer would get 1": right under the default NULL semantics
  (NULL = NULL is NULL, so IIF takes the false branch and returns 1). The seed has no NULL store_id, customer or
  ordered_at. Caveat: the Integration Service property TreatNullInComparisonOperatorsAs (LOW/HIGH) could change
  this. That comes from documentation; I have not tested it.

## 6. masterouter: "All 10 Master Outer joins keep the other side". CONFIRMED (with omissions)

- There are exactly 10 Master Outer joins: 6 enriched (JNR_ADD_CUSTOMERS, JNR_ADD_LOCATIONS, JNR_ADD_SUPPLIES,
  JNR_ORDERS_ITEMS_AGG, JNR_ADD_LOCATION_INFO, JNR_CUSTOMERS) and 4 core (JNR_ADD_SUPPLY_COST,
  JNR_ITEMS_SUPPLIES, JNR_ORDERS_ITEMS_AGG, JNR_CUSTOMERS_ORDERS). In every one, the master ports come from the
  main stream (items, orders, store-day KPIs or customers) and the detail ports from the lookup or aggregate side
  (p7.py). Confirmed.
- Semantics: a Master Outer join keeps every detail row plus the matching master rows and drops unmatched master
  rows. This comes from documentation, not a test.
- L3651/L3664/L3677: customers are the master, and LIFETIME_ORDERS_CL = IIF(ISNULL(…),0,…). Confirmed.
  L2227/L2366 (JNR_CUSTOMERS and PROSPECT): confirmed.
- "The seed data has no customers without orders": 0 customers without orders, 0 orders without a customer, and
  0 customers whose orders all lack items. Confirmed.
- 483 orders without items and 61,465 with items: confirmed by SQL. I traced row counts through both mappings.
  Every product has supplies and items, every item has a product and an order, and every customer has items.
  So ORDERS gets 61,465 rows (core: detail = AGG_ITEMS_BY_ORDER, L3949) and ORDER_FINANCIALS gets 61,465 (the
  Router passes all of them, problem 7). jaffle-shop's `main.orders` has 61,948.
- "One pair changes counts today": right for final **row** counts. The other joins change counts only in
  between (JNR_ADD_LOCATIONS adds 4 NULL-store rows that JNR_ADD_SUPPLIES drops again).
- L2061/L2385: 4 stores with no orders come back as rows with a NULL master side, and `NOT ISNULL(LOCATION_ID)`
  removes them. Confirmed.
- **Omission 1:** the same JNR_ORDERS_ITEMS_AGG (L1573) also feeds AGGTRANS and AGG_BY_LOCATION_DAY through the
  Router and Union. So it also changes aggregated counts. CUSTOMER_360.COUNT_LIFETIME_ORDERS is lower for 85
  customers, F_SCORE changes for 2, and FIRST/LAST_ORDERED_AT changes for 5 each. STORE_DAILY_KPIS.ORDERS_COUNT
  is lower on 319 store-days. (Money totals are not affected, because the dropped orders total 0.)
- **Omission 2 (PROSPECT):** "PROSPECT needs customers with no orders" is true, but it is not enough. Even with a
  Detail Outer join, COUNT_LIFETIME_ORDERS reaches L2366 uncleaned: L2256 passes COUNT_LIFETIME_ORDERS_IN
  through, and only v_ORDERS_CL (L2267) is set to 0 when NULL. So `COUNT_LIFETIME_ORDERS=0` would be NULL, the
  IIF would take the false branch, and the customer would land in STANDARD, not PROSPECT.

## 7. threshold: "A dollar rule applied to cents". CONFIRMED

- L1740 `ORDER_TOTAL >= 50`. Path: STG_ORDERS.ORDER_TOTAL (which holds cents, L613) → SQ_STG_ORDERS1 (L2578) →
  JNR_ORDERS_ITEMS_AGG (L2742) → EXP_ORDER_FINANCIALS (L2749) → SRT_FOR_CUSTOMER_SEQ (L2772) →
  EXP_CUSTOMER_ORDER_NUM (L2779) → SRT_BEFORE_ROUTER (L2796) → RTR (L2814). Confirmed.
- Orders with items: 61,465, with min order_total = 416 cents, so all of them are ≥ 50 and 61,465 of 61,465
  are HIGH. Orders with order_total < 50: 483, and all 483 have no items and order_total 0. That is the same
  set as the item-less orders. Confirmed.
- order_total ≥ 5000 among orders with items: 1,216 = 1.98% (1.96% of all 61,948). "2.0%" is right either way.

## 8. perishable: "The perishable rule doesn't match the data". CONFIRMED

- L504: `IIF(PERISHABLE = 'Y' OR PERISHABLE = '1', 1, 0)`. L10: PERISHABLE is varchar2(50). The seed CSV
  `raw_supplies.csv` holds "True" ×30 and "False" ×35.
- DuckDB test (v2.0.1): raw.raw_supplies.perishable is BOOLEAN. `perishable = 'Y' OR perishable = '1'` gives 30;
  `'Y'::boolean` and `'1'::boolean` are both true. The same rule on the text values
  (`cast(perishable as varchar)`) gives 0. 0 of 65 versus 30 of 65 is confirmed by test.
- "0 of 65" assumes the text in Oracle is "True"/"False", as in the CSV.

## 9. rundate: "Customer recency depends on a run-date setting". CONFIRMED, with a missing caveat

- L3104: `$$RUN_DATE` defaults to 12/31/2025 00:00:00. L2300/L2318 use DATE_DIFF(TRUNC($$RUN_DATE),
  TRUNC(LAST_ORDERED_AT),'DD'). The last seed order is 2025-08-31 18:46, which gives 122 days. L2341: ≤30 → 3,
  ≤90 → 2, else 1. L2366: CHAMPION needs RFM 333 and LOYAL needs R_SCORE=3. Confirmed under the default.
- **Missing caveat:** L3104 has `ISPARAM="YES"`, so this is a mapping parameter. The enriched session names a
  parameter file at L4554 (`…/SrcFiles/Enriched_Data_Mart_Parameter.txt`), and that file is not in the repo.
  If the file sets $$RUN_DATE, the default does not apply and the R_SCORE result can differ.
- Suggested addition: "The enriched session points at a parameter file (L4554) that we do not have. It may
  override this default."

## 10. truncate: "'Truncate target = NO', yet every table is emptied first". CONFIRMED

- 16 writers in total: staging 6, core 5, enriched 5. All 16 have "Truncate target table option" = NO (for
  example L919). All 16 target instances have Pre SQL `TRUNCATE TABLE STG.x` or `MART.x` (L535–550,
  L2389–2401, L3691–3703). No session overrides Pre SQL.
- Semantics: target Pre SQL runs against the target before the load, and the truncate option only controls
  whether the Integration Service truncates on its own. This comes from documentation.

## 11. connection: "The staging session has two sets of connections". CONFIRMED

- The reusable s_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL uses MART_Jaffleshop for all 6 writers and 7 readers (L888–985; L912 is an
  example). The task instance at L4579–4619 overrides them: STG_Jaffleshop for the 6 writers (L4580–4597) and
  RAW_Jaffleshop for the 7 readers (L4598–4618).
- "The override is what actually runs": a workflow task-instance override takes precedence over the reusable
  session's own connection. This comes from documentation, not a test.

## 12. instancename: "A target instance named differently from its table". CONFIRMED

- L2391 is INSTANCE ORDER_FINANCIALS1 with TRANSFORMATION_NAME ORDER_FINANCIALS. L1112 is the table. The session
  writer at L4466 uses SINSTANCENAME ORDER_FINANCIALS1. Across all 16 target instances, this is the only one
  whose name differs from its table.

## 13. default-group: "Rows that match no Router group are dropped". CONFIRMED

- L277 and L1741 are the DEFAULT1 groups, and their output ports (RTR_REGION *2 at L300–304, RTR_ORDER_VALUE_BAND
  *2 at L1797–1814) have no outgoing connectors (p10.py).
- REGION is EMEA, APAC or AMER for any TAX_RATE. A NULL rate falls through to AMER. The seed has 0 NULL
  order_total, and the Router input comes from matched master rows.
- Semantics: an unconnected default group drops its rows, and a NULL condition does not route. This comes from
  documentation (and assumes the default NULL comparison setting).

## 14. region: "Region is guessed from the tax rate". CONFIRMED

- L236 matches the description. The 6 seed tax rates are 0.06, 0.04, 0.0625, 0.075, 0.04 and 0.08, so the
  maximum is 8%, all 6 are AMER, and the APAC/EMEA branches are empty.
- L276: the G_APAC expression is `REGION = 'APAC'` followed by CR LF. The line break is outside the string
  literal, so it is harmless whitespace. Calling it "stray" is fine.

## 15. year: "Order dates pass through a 2-digit year". CONFIRMED

- L110 `TO_DATE(TO_CHAR(ORDERED_AT,'DD-MM-YY'),'DD-MM-YY')` drops the time of day. In PowerCenter's TO_DATE,
  `YY` takes the century from the current date (RR is the rounding variant). This comes from documentation.
  Running in 2024–2099 gives the right century for 2024–2025 data.

## 16. sorters: "15 Sorters: most change nothing, 3 matter". CONFIRMED

- 15 Sorters: 6 staging, 7 enriched, 2 core. All have Distinct = NO (L1434 is one). All Aggregators and Joiners
  have Sorted Input = NO.
- SRT_BY_CUSTOMER (L3554) feeds the core EXP_CUSTOMER_ORDER_NUM. SRT_FOR_CUSTOMER_SEQ (L1635) feeds the enriched
  EXP_CUSTOMER_ORDER_NUM. SRT_FOR_DISTINCT_CUSTOMER (L2091) feeds EXP_MARK_FIRST_CUSTOMER. These three
  transformations hold the only row-to-row state in the XML. Confirmed.

## 17. unused: "42 columns are read but never used". PARTLY WRONG

- Source Qualifier output ports with no outgoing connector: **42** in 12 Source Qualifiers (p10.py). Confirmed.
  Enriched SQ_STG_ORDERS L1232–1237 has all 6 money ports unconnected; only ORDER_ID, CUSTOMER_ID, LOCATION_ID
  and ORDERED_AT_DAY go on (L2606–2609). Confirmed.
- **Wrong:** "One join key is also unused (L485)". L485 is SKU1 in JNR_SUPPLIES_PRODUCTS, and it **is** used: the
  join condition at L488 is `SKU1 = SKU`. Only its output side has no connector.
- Wording: "read" is probably inaccurate. PowerCenter's generated default SELECT includes only the SQ ports
  that are connected downstream, so these 42 columns are most likely never fetched. This comes from
  documentation and I have not tested it.
- Suggested wording: "42 Source Qualifier ports are never connected to anything downstream. … Joiner port SKU1
  (L485) is used only in its join condition; its output is not connected."

## 18. names: "13 transformation names appear in both mart mappings". CONFIRMED

- 13 names are shared by enriched and core (p11.py), including AGG_SUPPLIES_BY_PRODUCT at L1441 and L3287. There
  are no folder-level reusable transformations, and staging shares no names with either mart mapping. 7 of the 13
  have different ports or logic in the two mappings, which strengthens the point.

## 19. twice: "Each staging table is described twice". CONFIRMED

- 6 STG_* targets (L44–89) and 6 STG_* sources (L1014–1059) match exactly on name, datatype, precision, scale and
  order (p12.py).

## 20. credential: "A plaintext database password in the command task". Structure CONFIRMED, credential content UNVERIFIABLE (by design)

- The TASK cmd_FL_JS_CREATE_RPT_VIEWS (type Command) spans L4058–4062. The file's only VALUEPAIR line is L4061,
  inside it. WORKFLOWLINK at L4622 runs it after s_FL_JS_MARTS_ENRICHED, the last session. Confirmed.
- No TARGET or SOURCE in the XML is a report view (no RPT/VW/VIEW names), so no mapping defines these views.
  Confirmed.
- "the command contains a database password" and "the report views it creates": I did **not** inspect the
  VALUEPAIR content, under the security rule. A boolean-only pattern check was blocked by the permission
  system and never ran, so I cannot independently confirm these two statements.

---

## Clean statements

1. "All 1,066 connectors point at a real instance and port": CONFIRMED. There are 1,066 CONNECTOR elements. Every
   FROM/TO instance exists in its mapping, every port exists on that instance, and the directions are right
   (from OUTPUT to INPUT).
2. "Every target column is fed by exactly one connector, and every transformation input is fed": CONFIRMED.
   No exceptions, and no input port has more than one connector.
3. "Every Aggregator output is either grouped by or aggregated": CONFIRMED. Every INPUT/OUTPUT Aggregator port is
   GROUPBY, and every OUTPUT expression starts with SUM, COUNT, MIN or MAX.
4. "No text column gets shorter on its way into a target": CONFIRMED. No string-to-string connector narrows, and no
   string expression refers to a wider string or a longer literal.
5. "No Source Qualifier has a SQL override, a filter or a custom join": CONFIRMED. Sql Query, User Defined Join,
   Source Filter, Pre SQL and Post SQL are empty, Select Distinct = NO, and there are no session-level SQ
   overrides.
6. "Every PC Source and PC Target is used by a mapping, and all 3 mappings are marked valid": CONFIRMED. All 12
   sources and 16 targets are instantiated, and all 3 mappings (and all 3 sessions) have ISVALID="YES".

## Semantics: what rests on what

| Claim | Basis |
|---|---|
| Variable ports evaluated in display order after inputs; a self-reference sees the previous row | Documentation (Informatica Transformation Guide, port order). Not testable here. High confidence. |
| Master Outer keeps all detail rows and drops unmatched master rows | Documentation. High. |
| Unconnected Router default group drops rows | Documentation. High. |
| IIF with a NULL condition takes the false branch; NULL = NULL is NULL | Documentation. Depends on TreatNullInComparisonOperatorsAs being at its default. Medium-high. |
| Truncate option NO versus target Pre SQL TRUNCATE | Documentation. High. |
| Task-instance connection override wins over the reusable session | Documentation. High. |
| DuckDB reads 'Y' and '1' as true against BOOLEAN | **Tested** on DuckDB 2.0.1: 30 of 65; text cast gives 0. |
| TO_DATE 'YY' takes the century from the current date | Documentation. Medium. |
| Unconnected SQ ports are left out of the default SELECT | Documentation. Medium (affects only the wording of problem 17). |
| Oracle NUMBER(p,0) rounds on insert | Oracle documentation. High. PowerCenter's own conversion not tested. |

## Seed facts (all re-run)

61,948 orders; 483 with order_total < 50 cents, which are exactly the 483 with no items; 61,465 with items, min
416 cents; 1,216 with order_total ≥ 5000; 61,296 with tax not a whole dollar; 45,658 with tax < 50 cents;
65 supplies, 30 perishable; 935 customers, 0 without orders; 6 stores, 4 without orders; last order
2025-08-31; max tax rate 0.08; jaffle-shop `main.orders` = 61,948 rows.

# Adversarial check of the 20 "problems in the input XML" and the 6 "clean" statements

Sources: the claims in `docs/assets/input-data.js` (problems + clean), the XML
`external/flowline-pwc-demo/FLOWLINE_DEMO_JAFFLESHOP.xml` (4,701 lines), jaffle-shop, and the seed data in
`q.duckdb` (schema `raw`, DuckDB 2.0.1, opened read-only).

Method: my own scripts in this folder. `h.py` is a helper built on pcxml.parse. `lineage.py` is a column-lineage
tracer. `p*.py` are one-off XML checks and `q.py` runs SQL. I did not open input_checks.py, build_input_data.py,
docs/*.html, agent_log.md or any transcript. Every grep of the XML went through `grep -v VALUEPAIR`.

Verdict scale: CONFIRMED (everything checkable is right), PARTLY WRONG (at least one statement is inaccurate
or overstated), WRONG, UNVERIFIABLE.

Every cited line number was printed and read. All of them hold what the text says, so I don't repeat
"line OK" below unless something is off.

---

## 1. swap: "Columns wired into the wrong target column, in 4 places". CONFIRMED

- L608–613 (STG_ORDERS): `SRT_ORDERS.SUBTOTAL -> SUBTOTAL_CENTS`, `TAX_PAID -> TAX_PAID_CENTS`,
  `ORDER_TOTAL -> ORDER_TOTAL_CENTS`, `SUBTOTAL_CENTS -> SUBTOTAL`, `TAX_PAID_CENTS -> TAX_PAID`,
  `ORDER_TOTAL_CENTS -> ORDER_TOTAL`. In EXP_ORDERS, SUBTOTAL = `SUBTOTAL_IN/100` (L111) and SUBTOTAL_CENTS =
  `SUBTOTAL_IN` (L114). So dollars go into the `*_CENTS` columns and cents into the dollar columns. Confirmed.
- L620–621 (STG_PRODUCTS): `PRODUCT_PRICE (PRICE/100) -> PRODUCT_PRICE_CENTS` and
  `PRODUCT_PRICE_CENTS (PRICE) -> PRODUCT_PRICE`. Confirmed.
- L2480–2482 (CUSTOMER_360): SPEND -> PRETAX, PRETAX -> TAX_PAID, TAX_PAID -> SPEND. Confirmed.
- L2542–2543 (PDP): PERISHABLE_SALES_FLAG -> MARGIN_PCT and MARGIN_PCT -> PERISHABLE_SALES_FLAG. Confirmed.
- "in 4 places": I checked every connector into a target whose source port name differs from the target
  column (p3.py). Exactly these 4 groups are swaps. The rest are harmless renames (ID -> CUSTOMER_ID,
  *_CL -> plain names). I also checked connectors into non-targets: the only name changes are the
  `*_RECAL -> SUBTOTAL/TAX_PAID/ORDER_TOTAL` renames at L4005–4007, which are not swaps.
- "joined by position": this is an inference, not something the XML records. It does fit all 4 cases: the
  upstream port order lines up with the target column order (for example SRT_ORDERS lists SUBTOTAL, TAX_PAID,
  ORDER_TOTAL, SUBTOTAL_CENTS… while the target lists SUBTOTAL_CENTS, TAX_PAID_CENTS, ORDER_TOTAL_CENTS,
  SUBTOTAL…).
- Suggested wording: "In each case the port order matches the target's column order, which suggests the
  ports were linked by position."

## 2. round: "Two of the swaps also lose data in the original database". PARTLY WRONG

- L1087: PERISHABLE_SALES_FLAG is `number(p,s)` with precision 1 and scale 0. L73: TAX_PAID_CENTS is
  `number(15,0)`. Confirmed.
- "61,296 of 61,948 orders have tax that is not a whole dollar". `select count(*) filter (where tax_paid % 100
  <> 0) from raw.raw_orders` gives 61,296 of 61,948. Confirmed.
- **Overstated:** "Tax in dollars (like 0.42) … so it becomes 0." Rounding to a whole number gives 0 only when
  the tax is under $0.50. The query `count(*) filter (where tax_paid < 50)` returns **45,658 orders → 0**, and
  `tax_paid >= 50` returns **16,290 orders → 1 to 6** (max tax is 594 cents). Of those, 225 are exactly x.50.
- MARGIN_PCT -> NUMBER(1,0): "becomes 0 or 1" holds for a ratio between 0 and 1. With the seed data and the
  swap, MARGIN_PCT works out to 1 − (supply cost in dollars)/(price in cents). That is 0.9965–0.9989 for every
  product (query over raw_products and raw_supplies), so **every PDP row would get 1**. The example "0.6543" is
  only an illustration.
- Missing: two more swaps put dollars into `number(15,0)` columns. STG_ORDERS.SUBTOTAL_CENTS (L72) gets
  dollar subtotals and STG_PRODUCTS.PRODUCT_PRICE_CENTS (L56) gets dollar prices. They lose nothing today only
  because every seed subtotal and price is a whole dollar (`subtotal % 100 <> 0` gives 0 rows, and prices are
  400–1400). So "two" is right for the seed data, but four columns are at risk in general. ORDER_TOTAL_CENTS
  is `number(12,2)` and loses nothing.
- Semantics: Oracle rounds to the column's scale when a value is inserted into NUMBER(p,0). I have not tested
  whether PowerCenter converts the value itself first (bulk mode, "Enable high precision" = NO at L1007). So
  "the database rounds it" is very likely right, but I have not tested it.
- Suggested wording: "Tax in dollars lands in TAX_PAID_CENTS, a NUMBER(15,0) column (L73), so it is rounded to
  a whole number: 0 for 45,658 orders and 1–6 for the other 16,290. MARGIN_PCT lands in PERISHABLE_SALES_FLAG,
  NUMBER(1,0) (L1087). With the seed data every margin is about 0.997, so the column is 1 on every row.
  SUBTOTAL_CENTS and PRODUCT_PRICE_CENTS are also NUMBER(15,0) and get dollars; they lose nothing today only
  because seed prices are whole dollars."

## 3. spread: "The staging swaps spread into the marts". CONFIRMED (with one note)

- My own lineage tracer (lineage.py) follows connectors, expression references, Router REF_FIELD and Union
  FIELDDEPENDENCY back from every mart target column. It flags columns that depend on STG_ORDERS
  {SUBTOTAL, TAX_PAID, ORDER_TOTAL and their *_CENTS columns} or STG_PRODUCTS {PRODUCT_PRICE, PRODUCT_PRICE_CENTS}.
  Result: **40 columns in 9 tables** (out of 130 mart columns). The column list is **identical** to the
  claim's list, table by table.
- L3534: `SUBTOTAL_RECAL = SUBTOTAL_CENTS/100` reaches ORDERS.SUBTOTAL through L4005 and L3783.
  STG_ORDERS.SUBTOTAL_CENTS holds dollars, so the result is 100 times too small. Confirmed. (ORDERS.TAX_PAID is
  worse, because TAX_PAID_CENTS was already rounded.)
- L1614: EFFECTIVE_TAX_RATE = TAX_PAID / SUBTOTAL. In the enriched mapping both inputs come from STG_ORDERS.TAX_PAID
  and SUBTOTAL (L2740–2741), which both hold cents and were not rounded. So the ratio is right. Confirmed.
- Note (missing, not wrong): the swap also changes 4 columns through the Router condition rather than through
  the data flow: ORDER_FINANCIALS.ORDER_VALUE_BAND, STORE_DAILY_KPIS.HIGH_VALUE_ORDERS, STORE_DAILY_KPIS.HIGH_VALUE_ORDERS_PCT
  and CUSTOMER_360.HIGH_VALUE_ORDERS. These are all "HIGH" or the full count because of problem 7. "Computed
  from" is accurate as a lineage statement, but readers may take the 40 as every column the swap affects.
- Also: some of the 40 come out numerically right anyway (EFFECTIVE_TAX_RATE). RFM_SEGMENT does not change
  today because R_SCORE is always 1, as problem 9 explains.

## 4. counter: "The per-customer order counter never restarts". CONFIRMED

- L3588: `v_PREV_CUSTOMER_ID = CUSTOMER_ID`. L3589: `v_ORDER_SEQUENCE = IIF(v_PREV_CUSTOMER_ID = CUSTOMER_ID,

  targets. Confirmed.

  variable that refers to itself sees the previous row's value, and a numeric variable starts at 0. This comes
  from documentation (Transformation Guide, port order), not a test. Given that, the comparison is TRUE on every
  row, so the counter runs 1…N in sorted order. The only exception would be a NULL CUSTOMER_ID: then NULL = NULL
  goes to the false branch and the counter resets to 1. The seed has no NULL customer (0 rows), and every row
  on this path comes from a matched join.
- jaffle-shop's `customer_order_number` is a `row_number()` per customer (orders.sql L68–71). Confirmed.

## 5. firstcustomer: "The first-customer flag is always 0". CONFIRMED

- L2124–2126 set v_PREV_LOCATION/DAY/CUSTOMER to the current row. L2127 compares them with the current row and
  returns 0 when they match. With the same port-order semantics, all three always match, so the flag is 0.
- L2004 `UNIQUE_CUSTOMERS = SUM(IS_FIRST_CUSTOMER)`, fed through L2940, reaches STORE_DAILY_KPIS through L2549.
  Confirmed.
- "Only a row with an empty location, day or customer would get 1": right under the default NULL semantics
  (NULL = NULL is NULL, so IIF takes the false branch and returns 1). The seed has no NULL store_id, customer or
  ordered_at. Caveat: the Integration Service property TreatNullInComparisonOperatorsAs (LOW/HIGH) could change
  this. That comes from documentation; I have not tested it.

## 6. masterouter: "All 10 Master Outer joins keep the other side". CONFIRMED (with omissions)

- There are exactly 10 Master Outer joins: 6 enriched (JNR_ADD_CUSTOMERS, JNR_ADD_LOCATIONS, JNR_ADD_SUPPLIES,
  JNR_ORDERS_ITEMS_AGG, JNR_ADD_LOCATION_INFO, JNR_CUSTOMERS) and 4 core (JNR_ADD_SUPPLY_COST,
  JNR_ITEMS_SUPPLIES, JNR_ORDERS_ITEMS_AGG, JNR_CUSTOMERS_ORDERS). In every one, the master ports come from the
  main stream (items, orders, store-day KPIs or customers) and the detail ports from the lookup or aggregate side
  (p7.py). Confirmed.
- Semantics: a Master Outer join keeps every detail row plus the matching master rows and drops unmatched master
  rows. This comes from documentation, not a test.
- L3651/L3664/L3677: customers are the master, and LIFETIME_ORDERS_CL = IIF(ISNULL(…),0,…). Confirmed.
  L2227/L2366 (JNR_CUSTOMERS and PROSPECT): confirmed.
- "The seed data has no customers without orders": 0 customers without orders, 0 orders without a customer, and
  0 customers whose orders all lack items. Confirmed.
- 483 orders without items and 61,465 with items: confirmed by SQL. I traced row counts through both mappings.
  Every product has supplies and items, every item has a product and an order, and every customer has items.
  So ORDERS gets 61,465 rows (core: detail = AGG_ITEMS_BY_ORDER, L3949) and ORDER_FINANCIALS gets 61,465 (the
  Router passes all of them, problem 7). jaffle-shop's `main.orders` has 61,948.
- "One pair changes counts today": right for final **row** counts. The other joins change counts only in
  between (JNR_ADD_LOCATIONS adds 4 NULL-store rows that JNR_ADD_SUPPLIES drops again).
- L2061/L2385: 4 stores with no orders come back as rows with a NULL master side, and `NOT ISNULL(LOCATION_ID)`
  removes them. Confirmed.
- **Omission 1:** the same JNR_ORDERS_ITEMS_AGG (L1573) also feeds AGGTRANS and AGG_BY_LOCATION_DAY through the
  Router and Union. So it also changes aggregated counts. CUSTOMER_360.COUNT_LIFETIME_ORDERS is lower for 85
  customers, F_SCORE changes for 2, and FIRST/LAST_ORDERED_AT changes for 5 each. STORE_DAILY_KPIS.ORDERS_COUNT
  is lower on 319 store-days. (Money totals are not affected, because the dropped orders total 0.)
- **Omission 2 (PROSPECT):** "PROSPECT needs customers with no orders" is true, but it is not enough. Even with a
  Detail Outer join, COUNT_LIFETIME_ORDERS reaches L2366 uncleaned: L2256 passes COUNT_LIFETIME_ORDERS_IN
  through, and only v_ORDERS_CL (L2267) is set to 0 when NULL. So `COUNT_LIFETIME_ORDERS=0` would be NULL, the
  IIF would take the false branch, and the customer would land in STANDARD, not PROSPECT.

## 7. threshold: "A dollar rule applied to cents". CONFIRMED

- L1740 `ORDER_TOTAL >= 50`. Path: STG_ORDERS.ORDER_TOTAL (which holds cents, L613) → SQ_STG_ORDERS1 (L2578) →
  JNR_ORDERS_ITEMS_AGG (L2742) → EXP_ORDER_FINANCIALS (L2749) → SRT_FOR_CUSTOMER_SEQ (L2772) →
  EXP_CUSTOMER_ORDER_NUM (L2779) → SRT_BEFORE_ROUTER (L2796) → RTR (L2814). Confirmed.
- Orders with items: 61,465, with min order_total = 416 cents, so all of them are ≥ 50 and 61,465 of 61,465
  are HIGH. Orders with order_total < 50: 483, and all 483 have no items and order_total 0. That is the same
  set as the item-less orders. Confirmed.
- order_total ≥ 5000 among orders with items: 1,216 = 1.98% (1.96% of all 61,948). "2.0%" is right either way.

## 8. perishable: "The perishable rule doesn't match the data". CONFIRMED

- L504: `IIF(PERISHABLE = 'Y' OR PERISHABLE = '1', 1, 0)`. L10: PERISHABLE is varchar2(50). The seed CSV
  `raw_supplies.csv` holds "True" ×30 and "False" ×35.
- DuckDB test (v2.0.1): raw.raw_supplies.perishable is BOOLEAN. `perishable = 'Y' OR perishable = '1'` gives 30;
  `'Y'::boolean` and `'1'::boolean` are both true. The same rule on the text values
  (`cast(perishable as varchar)`) gives 0. 0 of 65 versus 30 of 65 is confirmed by test.
- "0 of 65" assumes the text in Oracle is "True"/"False", as in the CSV.

## 9. rundate: "Customer recency depends on a run-date setting". CONFIRMED, with a missing caveat

- L3104: `$$RUN_DATE` defaults to 12/31/2025 00:00:00. L2300/L2318 use DATE_DIFF(TRUNC($$RUN_DATE),
  TRUNC(LAST_ORDERED_AT),'DD'). The last seed order is 2025-08-31 18:46, which gives 122 days. L2341: ≤30 → 3,
  ≤90 → 2, else 1. L2366: CHAMPION needs RFM 333 and LOYAL needs R_SCORE=3. Confirmed under the default.
- **Missing caveat:** L3104 has `ISPARAM="YES"`, so this is a mapping parameter. The enriched session names a
  parameter file at L4554 (`…/SrcFiles/Enriched_Data_Mart_Parameter.txt`), and that file is not in the repo.
  If the file sets $$RUN_DATE, the default does not apply and the R_SCORE result can differ.
- Suggested addition: "The enriched session points at a parameter file (L4554) that we do not have. It may
  override this default."

## 10. truncate: "'Truncate target = NO', yet every table is emptied first". CONFIRMED

- 16 writers in total: staging 6, core 5, enriched 5. All 16 have "Truncate target table option" = NO (for
  example L919). All 16 target instances have Pre SQL `TRUNCATE TABLE STG.x` or `MART.x` (L535–550,
  L2389–2401, L3691–3703). No session overrides Pre SQL.
- Semantics: target Pre SQL runs against the target before the load, and the truncate option only controls
  whether the Integration Service truncates on its own. This comes from documentation.

## 11. connection: "The staging session has two sets of connections". CONFIRMED

- The reusable s_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL uses MART_Jaffleshop for all 6 writers and 7 readers (L888–985; L912 is an
  example). The task instance at L4579–4619 overrides them: STG_Jaffleshop for the 6 writers (L4580–4597) and
  RAW_Jaffleshop for the 7 readers (L4598–4618).
- "The override is what actually runs": a workflow task-instance override takes precedence over the reusable
  session's own connection. This comes from documentation, not a test.

## 12. instancename: "A target instance named differently from its table". CONFIRMED

- L2391 is INSTANCE ORDER_FINANCIALS1 with TRANSFORMATION_NAME ORDER_FINANCIALS. L1112 is the table. The session
  writer at L4466 uses SINSTANCENAME ORDER_FINANCIALS1. Across all 16 target instances, this is the only one
  whose name differs from its table.

## 13. default-group: "Rows that match no Router group are dropped". CONFIRMED

- L277 and L1741 are the DEFAULT1 groups, and their output ports (RTR_REGION *2 at L300–304, RTR_ORDER_VALUE_BAND
  *2 at L1797–1814) have no outgoing connectors (p10.py).
- REGION is EMEA, APAC or AMER for any TAX_RATE. A NULL rate falls through to AMER. The seed has 0 NULL
  order_total, and the Router input comes from matched master rows.
- Semantics: an unconnected default group drops its rows, and a NULL condition does not route. This comes from
  documentation (and assumes the default NULL comparison setting).

## 14. region: "Region is guessed from the tax rate". CONFIRMED

- L236 matches the description. The 6 seed tax rates are 0.06, 0.04, 0.0625, 0.075, 0.04 and 0.08, so the
  maximum is 8%, all 6 are AMER, and the APAC/EMEA branches are empty.
- L276: the G_APAC expression is `REGION = 'APAC'` followed by CR LF. The line break is outside the string
  literal, so it is harmless whitespace. Calling it "stray" is fine.

## 15. year: "Order dates pass through a 2-digit year". CONFIRMED

- L110 `TO_DATE(TO_CHAR(ORDERED_AT,'DD-MM-YY'),'DD-MM-YY')` drops the time of day. In PowerCenter's TO_DATE,
  `YY` takes the century from the current date (RR is the rounding variant). This comes from documentation.
  Running in 2024–2099 gives the right century for 2024–2025 data.

## 16. sorters: "15 Sorters: most change nothing, 3 matter". CONFIRMED

- 15 Sorters: 6 staging, 7 enriched, 2 core. All have Distinct = NO (L1434 is one). All Aggregators and Joiners
  have Sorted Input = NO.
- SRT_BY_CUSTOMER (L3554) feeds the core EXP_CUSTOMER_ORDER_NUM. SRT_FOR_CUSTOMER_SEQ (L1635) feeds the enriched
  EXP_CUSTOMER_ORDER_NUM. SRT_FOR_DISTINCT_CUSTOMER (L2091) feeds EXP_MARK_FIRST_CUSTOMER. These three
  transformations hold the only row-to-row state in the XML. Confirmed.

## 17. unused: "42 columns are read but never used". PARTLY WRONG

- Source Qualifier output ports with no outgoing connector: **42** in 12 Source Qualifiers (p10.py). Confirmed.
  Enriched SQ_STG_ORDERS L1232–1237 has all 6 money ports unconnected; only ORDER_ID, CUSTOMER_ID, LOCATION_ID
  and ORDERED_AT_DAY go on (L2606–2609). Confirmed.
- **Wrong:** "One join key is also unused (L485)". L485 is SKU1 in JNR_SUPPLIES_PRODUCTS, and it **is** used: the
  join condition at L488 is `SKU1 = SKU`. Only its output side has no connector.
- Wording: "read" is probably inaccurate. PowerCenter's generated default SELECT includes only the SQ ports
  that are connected downstream, so these 42 columns are most likely never fetched. This comes from
  documentation and I have not tested it.
- Suggested wording: "42 Source Qualifier ports are never connected to anything downstream. … Joiner port SKU1
  (L485) is used only in its join condition; its output is not connected."

## 18. names: "13 transformation names appear in both mart mappings". CONFIRMED

- 13 names are shared by enriched and core (p11.py), including AGG_SUPPLIES_BY_PRODUCT at L1441 and L3287. There
  are no folder-level reusable transformations, and staging shares no names with either mart mapping. 7 of the 13
  have different ports or logic in the two mappings, which strengthens the point.

## 19. twice: "Each staging table is described twice". CONFIRMED

- 6 STG_* targets (L44–89) and 6 STG_* sources (L1014–1059) match exactly on name, datatype, precision, scale and
  order (p12.py).

## 20. credential: "A plaintext database password in the command task". Structure CONFIRMED, credential content UNVERIFIABLE (by design)

- The TASK cmd_FL_JS_CREATE_RPT_VIEWS (type Command) spans L4058–4062. The file's only VALUEPAIR line is L4061,
  inside it. WORKFLOWLINK at L4622 runs it after s_FL_JS_MARTS_ENRICHED, the last session. Confirmed.
- No TARGET or SOURCE in the XML is a report view (no RPT/VW/VIEW names), so no mapping defines these views.
  Confirmed.
- "the command contains a database password" and "the report views it creates": I did **not** inspect the
  VALUEPAIR content, under the security rule. A boolean-only pattern check was blocked by the permission
  system and never ran, so I cannot independently confirm these two statements.

---

## Clean statements

1. "All 1,066 connectors point at a real instance and port": CONFIRMED. There are 1,066 CONNECTOR elements. Every
   FROM/TO instance exists in its mapping, every port exists on that instance, and the directions are right
   (from OUTPUT to INPUT).
2. "Every target column is fed by exactly one connector, and every transformation input is fed": CONFIRMED.
   No exceptions, and no input port has more than one connector.
3. "Every Aggregator output is either grouped by or aggregated": CONFIRMED. Every INPUT/OUTPUT Aggregator port is
   GROUPBY, and every OUTPUT expression starts with SUM, COUNT, MIN or MAX.
4. "No text column gets shorter on its way into a target": CONFIRMED. No string-to-string connector narrows, and no
   string expression refers to a wider string or a longer literal.
5. "No Source Qualifier has a SQL override, a filter or a custom join": CONFIRMED. Sql Query, User Defined Join,
   Source Filter, Pre SQL and Post SQL are empty, Select Distinct = NO, and there are no session-level SQ
   overrides.
6. "Every PC Source and PC Target is used by a mapping, and all 3 mappings are marked valid": CONFIRMED. All 12
   sources and 16 targets are instantiated, and all 3 mappings (and all 3 sessions) have ISVALID="YES".

## Semantics: what rests on what

| Claim | Basis |
|---|---|
| Variable ports evaluated in display order after inputs; a self-reference sees the previous row | Documentation (Informatica Transformation Guide, port order). Not testable here. High confidence. |
| Master Outer keeps all detail rows and drops unmatched master rows | Documentation. High. |
| Unconnected Router default group drops rows | Documentation. High. |
| IIF with a NULL condition takes the false branch; NULL = NULL is NULL | Documentation. Depends on TreatNullInComparisonOperatorsAs being at its default. Medium-high. |
| Truncate option NO versus target Pre SQL TRUNCATE | Documentation. High. |
| Task-instance connection override wins over the reusable session | Documentation. High. |
| DuckDB reads 'Y' and '1' as true against BOOLEAN | **Tested** on DuckDB 2.0.1: 30 of 65; text cast gives 0. |
| TO_DATE 'YY' takes the century from the current date | Documentation. Medium. |
| Unconnected SQ ports are left out of the default SELECT | Documentation. Medium (affects only the wording of problem 17). |
| Oracle NUMBER(p,0) rounds on insert | Oracle documentation. High. PowerCenter's own conversion not tested. |

## Seed facts (all re-run)

61,948 orders; 483 with order_total < 50 cents, which are exactly the 483 with no items; 61,465 with items, min
416 cents; 1,216 with order_total ≥ 5000; 61,296 with tax not a whole dollar; 45,658 with tax < 50 cents;
65 supplies, 30 perishable; 935 customers, 0 without orders; 6 stores, 4 without orders; last order
2025-08-31; max tax rate 0.08; jaffle-shop `main.orders` = 61,948 rows.
